::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Aug. 21st, 1858  
**From:** Sackville College  
**Manuscript:** MS UCLA collection 100 box 119/10
:::

My dear Miss Yonge,

[I](people/person_1087.qmd)leave [my wife](people/person_1815.qmd) to answer the part of your letter which concerns her.

Yes: I had read your [memoirs of Madame Lamourous](cmy_books/cmybook_31.qmd); and [our Sisters](organizations/other_45.qmd) have just been reading it at meal time in the Refectory.[^1] But I am bound to tell you that I asked [our Mother](people/person_1816.qmd) to mark out other observations of yours about the faith &c of the subject of your memoirs: which, to tell you the truth, I was sorry to see there, both in a literary and religious point of view.

I read the other day—I am ashamed to say for the first time,—[Heartsease](cmy_books/cmybook_19.qmd): and I am not sure but that I like <u>John</u>—at least as he appears in the former half of the book, better than any other of your characters. I wish you could have given us more about him.

Will you let me say one thing more? I confess I was very sorry that at the time when S. Margaret’s was at the height of its unpopularity, you refused a paper which a very good friend [of] yours, sent you about it. I knew that, under <u>God</u>, we should weather the storm well enough, but I felt deeply grateful to those who helped us then. Yet I would rather have had the feeling of gratitude to the [Monthly Packet](organizations/other_52.qmd), than to the [Penny Post](organizations/other_96.qmd). Now, thank <u>God</u>, I think we are all the better for the shake. And a very safe set of people, namely, the [Guild of S. Alban’s](organizations/other_24.qmd) sent a long address to our Sisters the other day, filled with all manner of laudation.

Do not think that this is said unkindly; for I assure you I have a deep feeling of obligation to you for what you have done by your books. I hope that, before long, we may have a successor to [the Heir of Redcliffe](cmy_books/cmybook_15.qmd), and to Heartsease.

Believe me I remain,

Yours very truly,

J. M. Neale

---

[^1]: *Marie Thérèse de Lamourous, Foundress of the House of La Miséricorde, at Bordeaux: A Biography*, abridged from the French by the author of *The Heir of Redclyffe*  (London: Parker 1858).
